# Plan: commit-attribution

Goal: Bind every commit to the initiative that produced it, exactly and at commit time, and spend that primitive on two gaps that share it. Gap 1 (staleness): several initiatives share one worktree and one branch, so any session's push carries other initiatives' commits and their records never learn their work shipped. Gap 2 (review): closing an initiative is today an unconditional append — nothing rechecks that the execution was right, and a reviewer with no diff can only re-read the record's own prose and confirm it. SETTLED AT 1.1 (D4): the binding lives in a `Sofar-Initiative:` COMMIT TRAILER and is READ from git — never recorded as an event, never inferred. That keeps record-hygiene D1 intact (logging git makes the record un-settleable) and clears record-integrity D6, which rejected per-commit attribution because it needed state the record must not keep. sofar stores nothing about commits; git carries the fact and sofar reads it, exactly as it already reads push state.

Progress: 1 done, 2 dropped, 18 remaining

## Phase 2 — Write and read the trailer [pending] — 0/4 done

- [ ] 2.1 DECIDE who writes the trailer and how it is made hard to forget. The agent must emit it at commit time, so the instruction belongs in the sofar protocol block that every session already receives — but an instruction alone will be forgotten, and a forgotten trailer is a silent unattributed commit. Weigh a `sofar` subcommand that prints the line, a commit template, and a prepare-commit-msg hook. Reliability is the whole design; this is where it actually leaks.
- [ ] 2.2 Read path in core/git.ts alongside readGitState: walk commits, parse the trailer, group shas by initiative. Keep the file's standing rule — it reads FILES, no subprocess, inside the 100ms shim budget (speed T2). A `git log` walk is a subprocess and a graph walk, so decide honestly whether this belongs on the hook path at all or only in on-demand commands.
- [ ] 2.3 Squash-merge fallback: `git merge --squash` indents the original message four spaces, so the trailer parser reads empty and a shipped initiative reports as un-shipped. The slug is still in the body verbatim — scan for it as a fallback, which is still reading git rather than guessing. Details and the false-negative direction are in repo memory.
- [ ] 2.4 doctor: commits reachable on the branch carrying no trailer and no recovered fallback — 1.3's surface, and the honest accounting of what the mechanism missed.

## Phase 3 — Derive shipped state (gap 1: staleness) [pending] — 0/3 done

- [ ] 3.1 Given the initiative's trailer-derived sha set, answer shipped-ness with `git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> <remote ref>`. Decide the behaviour when the remote ref is stale, absent, or never fetched: say "unknown", never guess "unpushed".

## Phase 4 — The review step (gap 2) [pending] — 0/5 done

- [ ] 4.1 DECIDE review granularity and who pays. Phase boundaries fit a session (3-5 tasks, warm memory, cheap fixes); close-only asks one session to audit 25 tasks at maximum surface and coldest memory. Each review costs a real session, so also fix the size threshold below which an initiative pays nothing — blanket application on a 3-task initiative is how this becomes ceremony.
- [ ] 4.2 The evidence packet, rendered from the record (a projection — templates dir only): the phase's diff from its trailer-derived sha set, the tasks claimed done, the decisions IN FORCE when that work happened, the rejected approaches, and any guard violations. Without a diff the reviewer re-reads the record's own prose and confirms it — the packet IS the review.
- [ ] 4.3 The instruction half: NAME the skills (`/code-review`, `/simplify`) rather than describing bug-hunting in prose — "check for bugs and edge cases" buys a paragraph of reassurance, a named skill buys a real review. sofar ships zero analysis code and makes zero model calls (SPEC §Architectural invariants); it emits the prompt and records the verdict.
- [ ] 4.4 The verdict event: what was found, what is still open, and whether surviving findings become tasks in the plan. A review that can only ever emit "looks good" is a rubber stamp — the verdict must be able to be "no".
- [ ] 4.5 Keep review DECOUPLED from marking done. If passing the review is what lets a session go home, the reviewing agent has an incentive to pass and will find nothing. Review emits findings; close reads them; they are separate steps.

## Phase 5 — Close gate + contracts [pending] — 0/5 done

- [ ] 5.1 Mechanical tier at close, no model needed: tasks still pending/active while closing `done`, phases never resolved, tasks claiming files no file_touched event ever saw, guard violations never addressed, a next_action left dangling. - [ ] 5.2 The override is an EVENT, never silent. A hard refusal on a solo tool grows a --force and the flag becomes the habit; "closed with 3 tasks pending, overridden" rendered in the digest forever is what keeps it honest.
- [ ] 5.3 `dropped` gets the review too — arguably needs it more, since half-built abandoned work is a bigger landmine than finished work, and today `dropped` demands only a prose reason.
